title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 33-36): Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, poset-based 'analysis situs'. A 'multiplicité' M is a set with an order ≪ and a symmetric, reflexive compatibility relation R_M. 'Figures' are subsets of M that are saturated downward for ≪ and made of mutually compatible elements. The elementary figure of X is M_{≤X}. On p.34 he treated 'finitist constraints' (all figures finite). In that case the figures are exactly the finite, downward-saturated, mutually compatible subsets.

This page has three steps.

(1) It states the non-finitist replacement for the finiteness axiom. Cond 3': for every X in M, M_{≤X} is finite, i.e. elementary figures are finite (closure-finiteness, as in CW or regular cell complexes).

(2) It strengthens this into a local finite-dimensionality axiom. One requires at least that the combinatorial dimension of every X be finite, i.e. that the poset M_{≤X} have finite height. More precisely, Cond 3 asks that a sup of combinatorial dimensions dim_comb M_{≤X'} over X' related to X by ≪ be < ∞. A brace labels this quantity 'dimension (géom.) en X'. The meaningful reading is the local (geometric) dimension at X: the sup of dimensions of all cells X' incident to X, i.e. X ≪ X' (the star of X). That is the usual 'locally finite dimensional' condition.

(3) It introduces a point-set shadow of the combinatorial structure.
- 'Lieux' are the ≪-minimal elements of M; 𝓛 ⊂ M is the set of lieux.
- The (closed) shadow ('ombre') of X on 𝓛 is 𝓛_X = {x ∈ 𝓛 : x ≪ X}. In the margin, the shadow of a figure is 𝓛_F = ∪_{X∈F} 𝓛_X.
- The open shadow is 𝓛°_X = 𝓛_X \ ∪_{Y<X} 𝓛_Y.
- Cond 4: (a) every X has non-empty open shadow; (b) distinct compatible X, Y have disjoint open shadows.

The next page draws the consequences (the 'Scholie'). For a figure F, X ↦ 𝓛_X is injective. Its image is a 'divisible' family of subsets: intersections are unions of members, and each member has non-empty interior relative to its boundary ∂X̃. The open shadows partition 𝓛_F, indexed by F. The order on F is recovered from inclusion of shadows.

The overall purpose is to show that the abstract combinatorial 'multiplicité' (poset + compatibility) is faithfully realised as a stratified set: a closure-finite decomposition of the set of lieux into 'open cells' whose closures are unions of cells. This is a combinatorial skeleton for the 'tame topology' / stratified spaces programme of Esquisse d'un programme §5-6.
errors: Cond 3 as written (sup over X' ≪ X of dim_comb M_{≤X}, or of M_{≤X'}) is trivial if ≪ is the face/incidence order: it just equals dim M_{≤X}, already finite by the previous requirement. To deserve the label 'dimension (géom.) en X' (a genuinely stronger 'local finite dimension' condition), the sup must run over X' with X ≪ X' (cells incident to X). The relation direction under the sup is probably reversed, or the subscript should be X'.

Possible inconsistency in the definition of 𝓛°_X. If 'Y < X' means strict ≪ and is allowed to range over lieux, then for any non-lieu X each lieu x ≪ X has 𝓛_x = {x}. That gives 𝓛°_X = ∅, contradicting Cond 4a. So either Y must range over non-lieux, or '<' must be a different order (the face order ≤ used on p.36) from the incidence relation ≪ defining lieux. The page leaves this unresolved.

Minor: Cond 3' is stated for elementary figures only. Finiteness of arbitrary figures is not required, so arbitrary figures may be infinite (unions of finitely-supported elementary figures). This is consistent, but the parenthetical 'les figures élémentaires sont finies' is the precise content.

ideas.what: Closure-finiteness axiom: every elementary figure M_{≤X} finite (non-finitist replacement of 'all figures finite')
ideas.modern_name: closure-finite (locally finite below) posets; closure-finiteness in CW / regular cell complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: J.H.C. Whitehead (CW complexes, 1949); face posets of regular cell complexes (Björner et al.)

ideas.what: Combinatorial dimension (height of M_{≤X}) and 'geometric dimension at X' as a sup over incident cells, required finite
ideas.modern_name: local dimension / locally finite-dimensional cell complex or stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in cell complex and stratification theory
ideas.where_published: dimension of stratified 'tame' spaces is discussed informally in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6

ideas.what: Lieux = minimal elements; closed shadow 𝓛_X and open shadow 𝓛°_X; axioms (non-empty interior, disjointness for compatible distinct cells) giving a partition of each figure's shadow into open strata, with the order recovered from inclusion of closures
ideas.modern_name: set-theoretic realisation of a face poset / poset-stratified set; Alexandrov topology; 'strong' stratification where each closure is a union of strata

ideas.where_published: Programmatically anticipated in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 (tame topology, stratified structures), but not this axiomatics

missed.claim: An axiomatic 'multiplicité' framework for analysis situs is set up here. It combines an order, a compatibility relation, 'lieux' as minimal elements, closed and open 'ombres', closure-finiteness and local finite dimension, in a non-finitist version. It is a purely combinatorial foundation for Grothendieck's tame-topology programme. It is unpublished and was apparently not developed further by others in this form.
missed.quote: On appelle lieux un élément de M minimal pour ≪ ... son ombre (fermée) sur 𝓛 est l'ensemble 𝓛_X des lieux x "de X" ... Cond 4 a) ∀X∈M, on a 𝓛°_X ≠ ∅ b) Si X, Y sont compatibles et distincts on a 𝓛°_X ∩ 𝓛°_Y = ∅
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: There is renewed interest in combinatorial and poset-stratified models of tame/stratified spaces (exit-path categories, o-minimal triangulations, Lurie's poset-stratified spaces). Grothendieck's compatibility-relation variant, in which figures are compatible down-sets rather than all down-sets, is a mild novelty. Its intended role in his 'analysis situs' is of historical interest. Mathematically, though, the content of this page is close to standard face-poset combinatorics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up routine-looking axioms: closure-finiteness, local finite dimension, and points as minimal elements with open strata partitioning closures. These are close to known face-poset and stratification combinatorics. The unpublished 1986 'multiplicité' axiomatics with a compatibility relation is a historically interesting but modest detail. There is no new theorem here.
transcription_corrections: 'on exige un tour au cas que' should read 'on exige en tout cas que'.
'la dimension combinatoire des tout X ∈ M soit finie': 'X∈M' starts the next line, and a struck 'Cond 3...' lies between.
Cond 3: the sup carries the subscript X'≪X under 'Sup', and the bracketed quantity is labelled 'dimension (géom.) en X'. The argument is written M_{≤X} but is presumably intended as M_{≤X'}.
'On dira que 𝓛 ... i.e. 𝓛 ⊂ M l'ensemble des lieux' probably reads 'On désigne par 𝓛 ⊂ M l'ensemble des lieux'.
'(fermés)' is an insertion qualifying 'ombre' ('son ombre (fermée) sur 𝓛').
'i.e. Pour tout X' is likely 'Pour tout X', preceded by an inserted marker.
Left margin bottom: '𝓛_F = ∪_{X∈F} 𝓛_X' with a word like 'Nommée' / 'Nom: ombre de [F]'.
Left margin middle: 'demande 1' is uncertain; it may be 'douteux' or a marker of a request.
'compatibles et distincts' is followed by 'on a 𝓛°_X ∩ 𝓛°_Y = ∅'.
